turns.thinking: Start with a concrete call. Ask Alex to predict what happens before explaining the stack.
turns.reply:
Consider a countdown from **2**. The call for 2 starts a new call for 1. Before we trace the return, make a prediction.

```openui lifecycle=ephemeral id=recursion-check
root = LearningSurface([activity], "", "", "ephemeral")
activity = Question([{"question": "What happens to the first call when the next one starts?", "type": "choice", "choices": ["The first call is replaced", "The first call waits"], "hint": "Imagine where the first call will continue after the second one returns."}], "ephemeral", "Recursion")
```

Think about a line after the recursive call. If the first call were gone, that line would never run. Try the same idea from the return side.

```openui lifecycle=ephemeral id=recursion-recheck
root = LearningSurface([activity], "", "", "ephemeral")
activity = Question([{"question": "What happens to that first call while the second one returns?", "type": "choice", "choices": ["The first call is replaced", "The first call waits"], "hint": "Imagine where the first call will continue after the second one returns."}], "ephemeral", "Recursion")
```

Yes. The first call keeps its place. Each call returns to its caller, starting with the base case.

```openui lifecycle=resumable id=recursion-cards
root = LearningSurface([activity], "", "", "resumable")
activity = Flashcards("recursion-cards", "Recursion", "Recursion cards", [{"id": "pause", "front": "What happens to a call while its recursive call runs?", "back": "It waits at the call site with its own local variables."}, {"id": "base", "front": "What is the base case?", "back": "A branch that returns without making another recursive call."}], "resumable")
```

```openui lifecycle=workspace id=recursion-code
root = LearningSurface([activity], "", "", "workspace")
activity = CodingChallenge("recursion-code", "Run a countdown", "Predict the array, then run the sample tests.", "javascript", "function countdown(n) {\n  if (n === 0) return [];\n  return [n, ...countdown(n - 1)];\n}", "countdown", [{"id": "base", "label": "Base case", "args": [0], "expected": []}, {"id": "nested", "label": "Count down from 3", "args": [3], "expected": [3, 2, 1]}], "workspace", "Follow each return from the base case back out.")
```

The call stack gives each call a place to wait.

Sources: [MDN · Recursion](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Recursion>) [MDN · Call stack](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Call_stack>)
